meta.title: Order Processing Manual
meta.subtitle: The lifecycle of a work order, from creation to handover
meta.$conventions:
This manual follows a single work order through the shop and the workshop, in the order the work actually happens. Read it front to back once; afterwards each chapter stands alone as a reference for that step.

Every screenshot is marked with numbered callouts. A number always indicates something you do: a control to click, a field to type into, or a choice to make. Numbers in the surrounding text refer to those callouts. Nothing is marked merely to draw the eye.

Under each step heading you will find the application (Shop or Workshop) and the page address, so you can confirm you are in the right place before acting.

$glossary.Work order: An order for custom tailoring, as opposed to a sales order for a ready-made item off the shelf.
$glossary.Garment: One physical piece. An order may contain several, and each is tracked independently through production.
$glossary.Brova: A trial garment made for the customer to try on before the remaining pieces are produced.
$glossary.Final: A finished garment for the customer to keep, as distinct from a brova.
$glossary.Parked: Held deliberately and not worked on. Finals are parked while a brova is awaiting the customer's verdict.
$glossary.Trip: One journey between the shop and the workshop. The first production run is trip 1; each return for alteration increases the number.
$glossary.Dispatch: Sending garments from one side to the other. They remain in transit until the receiving side records them.
$glossary.Cashier processing: The point at which a cashier either records a payment or confirms the order without one. Until this happens the order cannot be sent to the workshop.
$glossary.Primary account: A customer in their own right.
$glossary.Secondary account: A customer belonging to a family, linked to a primary account and carrying a stated relation to it.

chapters.title: Creating a work order
chapters.intro: A work order is created on the New Work Order form, a five-step wizard: customer details, garments and measurements, fabric, shelf items, and a final review. No record is written until the review step is confirmed. This chapter covers the customer step, including the procedure when the mobile number is already held on file.

chapters.title: Cashier processing
chapters.intro: Every confirmed work order enters the cashier's Pending queue. The order cannot be dispatched to the workshop until a cashier has processed it here. Note that the gate is opened by the act of processing, not by payment: an order confirmed without payment is free to proceed.

chapters.title: Dispatching to the workshop
chapters.intro: Dispatch records garments leaving the showroom for the workshop. Only orders already processed by a cashier appear in this queue.

chapters.title: Receiving at the workshop
chapters.intro: Garments in transit are listed on the workshop Receiving page. Recording receipt transfers responsibility for the garment to the workshop.

chapters.title: Scheduling production
chapters.intro: Cutting cannot begin until every production stage has an assigned owner. Assignment is recorded in the scheduler.

chapters.title: Dispatching back to the showroom
chapters.intro: A garment that has passed quality check is available for return to the showroom.

steps.title: Dispatch the garment to the showroom

chapters.title: Receiving at the showroom
chapters.intro: Garments returning from the workshop are listed on the Receiving Brova / Final page.

chapters.title: Handover to the customer
chapters.intro: Handover is recorded from the cashier's order page. Handover is not gated on payment: whether to release a garment against an outstanding balance is a matter for staff judgment.
